source_text: Qua ergo ratione indignum esset, non imagine Dei, quia animae quam carnis diversa substantia est, sed mancipio dissolubili imaginis Dei, quod indignum non fuerat conditu ipsius Dei? Fecit ergo corpora Deus, distinxit sexum corporum Deus, fecit membra genitalia Deus, indidit affectum quo sibi haec corpora miscerentur Deus, dedit etiam vim seminum Deus, operatur in secretis naturae de materia seminum Deus: nihil autem malum, nihil reum facit Deus.
pass_a_gloss: By what reason therefore would it be unworthy, not for the image of God, because the substance of the soul is diverse from that of the flesh, but for the dissoluble slave of the image of God, what had not been unworthy for the founding of God himself? God therefore made bodies, God distinguished the sex of bodies, God made the genital members, God put in the affection by which these bodies would be mingled with one another, God also gave the force of seeds, God works in the secrets of nature from the matter of seeds: but God makes nothing evil, nothing guilty.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: On what grounds, then, would something be unworthy, not of God’s image—for the soul’s substance differs from the flesh’s—but of the perishable servant of God’s image, when it was not unworthy of God himself to create it? God made bodies; God distinguished their sexes; God made the reproductive organs; God implanted the feeling through which these bodies unite; God also gave power to seeds; God works in nature’s hidden places from the material of seeds. But God makes nothing evil and nothing guilty.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
